newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.

text.p: Leading German and British stocks closed at record highs on Monday, boosted by another strong start on Wall Street where investors are confident U.S. inflation is under control.

The German DAX index, underpinned by the firmer dollar which makes German exports more attractive, ended up 33.91 points at 2,629.87, only just below the session high of 2,630.32. Frankfurt floor trade ended about 30 points above its previous intra-day peak, set on Friday.
London stocks also scored a record close at 3977.2, up 9.3 points on the day and some eight points up on their Friday intraday high, but off Monday's opening peak of 3,980.8.

Dealers said cautious investors were still sitting back to see if New York could repeat its 1.15 percent rise of Friday, when the Dow closed at a record 5,838.52 as treasuries powered ahead. By the time London closed the Dow was up 32.55 points at 5871,07, or more than half a percentage point.
The psychological 4,000 level looked a probability for the FTSE in the near term, London dealers said, though volumes remained thin.

"We saw a squeeze up on the opening after Friday's euphoria and then it came back. It feels like it will still go to 4,000 this week but we will have to have Wall Street very strong to get it there," said one trader.
Analysts warned that one element which could take the wind out of London shares is political uncertainty in Britain ahead of the general election which must be held before May 1997.

In Paris leading shares, helped by the stronger Wall Street, closed up 5.8 points or a quarter of a percent, extending last week's 3.77 percent advance. Dealers said other positive factors were rising bond prices and a stronger franc.

On the Milan bourse, Olivetti shares were automatically suspended after plunging 10 percent following news that the crisis-hit Italian information technology group's chief executive was under preliminary investigation by magistrates.
In foreign exchange, the dollar dollar lost its struggle to keep firmly above 1.51 marks, dragged down by the feeling that no U.S. interest rate rise was on the cards near-term, dealers said.

The dollar fell below 1.24 Swiss francs and hovered around 1.51 marks in late trade but key support levels remained untouched. Against the yen, the dollar also slipped to session lows in line with general dollar sales.
Support lent by the Iraq crisis was fading, dealers said, and the view was growing that U.S. interest rates would be left unchanged at the September 24 meeting of the Federal Open Markets Committee.

"The dollar is likely to struggle this week to hold on to its recent gains," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Most importantly, interest rate support is waning." Meanwhile, buoyant oil prices eased on Monday after Iraq appeared to defuse a military standoff with Washington by suspending attacks on U.S. warplanes patrolling Iraqi no fly zones.

November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend were trading down 73 cents at $22.40 a barrel in late Europe on Monday. Brent for October hit a five-year post Gulf War peak at $24.39 a barrel last Thursday after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. planes and Washington sent more weaponry to the region.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5105 marks and 110.13 yen compared with late Friday's 1.5112 marks and 110.32 yen.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 9.3 points higher at 3,977.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 5.82 at 2,086.19.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 33.91 at 2,629.87.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $382.70, compared with Friday's London close of $383.10. Silver ended two cents lower at $5.05.
